script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

SARAH (early 30s, bookish, determined) types on her laptop, surrounded by papers and books. A phone call comes through. She hesitates, then answers.

SARAH
(into phone)
Hello?

MAX (mid-30s, confident, charming)
Hey, it's Max. I hope I'm not disturbing you.

Sarah looks at the clock. 10:30 PM.

SARAH
(skeptically)
Max, it is late.

MAX
I know, but I couldn't resist the urge to call. I've been thinking about the job you mentioned earlier today. I think I can make a difference there.

Sarah sighs, leaning back in her chair.

SARAH
Max, I appreciate your enthusiasm, but I'm not sure they'll take you on without a degree in your field.

Max leans against the doorframe of Sarah's apartment.

MAX
You're right, I don't have a degree in environmental science, but I've got a solid background in business, and I've been following that organization closely for years. I could bring a fresh perspective, and I'm willing to learn the rest on the job.

Sarah looks up from her laptop, considering his words.

SARAH
I'll talk to them, but I can't make any promises, Max.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Sarah sits at a table, reading through files on her laptop. Max enters, carrying two coffees.

MAX
(setting down the coffees)
Hey, Sarah. Thanks for meeting me here. I brought us some coffee.

SARAH
(looking up from her laptop)
Max, this isn't a date.

MAX
(smiling)
I know, I know. Just trying to be nice. I brought you a decaf, by the way.

They both laugh. Sarah opens the files on her laptop and begins to explain her concerns to Max.

MAX
Sarah, have you considered the value of practical experience versus a piece of paper? I understand that a degree can be important, but it's not the only factor. And in my case, I've got a proven track record of success in business. I believe I can apply that knowledge to the environmental sector and make a real impact.

SARAH
(nodding)
I agree that experience is valuable, but I also have to consider the needs of the organization. They're looking for someone with a strong background in environmental science.

MAX
But Sarah, think about it. I've been following their work closely for years. I know their mission, their challenges, and their opportunities. I've got a solid understanding of the industry and the issues they face. I could bring a unique perspective to the team, one that could help them tackle those challenges more effectively.

SARAH
(leaning back in her chair)
Max, I like your enthusiasm, and I appreciate your confidence. I'll take your points into consideration, but I can't make any promises. The hiring manager is very particular about the qualifications they're looking for.

INT. OFFICE - DAY

Sarah sits across from the hiring manager, JENNIFER (late 40s, no-nonsense, focused), who listens intently as Sarah presents Max's case.

JENNIFER
(leaning forward)
Sarah, I understand your perspective, but my hands are tied. This position requires a strong background in environmental science. I can't risk hiring someone without the necessary qualifications.

SARAH
I understand, Jennifer. But I believe Max has a unique set of skills and experience that could benefit the organization. He's been following our work closely for years and has a solid background in business. He's willing to learn the rest on the job, and I believe he could bring a fresh perspective to the team.

JENNIFER
(skeptical)
Sarah, I appreciate your advocacy, but I've got to consider the needs of the organization. We simply can't afford to take a risk on an unproven candidate.

SARAH
(pleading)
Jennifer, please consider it. Max has a proven track record of success in business, and he's genuinely passionate about making a difference in the environmental sector. He's willing to learn, and I believe he could bring value to the team.

JENNIFER
(sighs)
Alright, Sarah. I'll bring him in for an interview. But I can't make any promises.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Sarah and Max sit across from each other, both with smiles on their faces.

MAX
(leaning back in his chair)
Thanks, Sarah. I really appreciate your advocacy.

SARAH
(smiling)
I believe in you, Max. And I think you've got a real chance here.

MAX
(nodding)
I won't let you down.

SARAH
(leaning forward)
I know you won't. Now, let's focus on preparing for the interview. What do you need from me?

INT. OFFICE - DAY

Max sits across from Jennifer during the interview. He answers her questions with confidence and passion, discussing his background in business and his enthusiasm for the environmental sector.

JENNIFER
(leaning forward)
Max, I'm impressed. You've got a solid understanding of the industry and the challenges we face. And I can see that you're genuinely passionate about making a difference. But I still have one concern. How do you plan to tackle the learning curve in a new field?

MAX
(smiling)
Jennifer, I understand that there will be a learning curve, but I'm confident in my ability to adapt and learn quickly. I'll be working closely with the team, and I'll be taking advantage of every resource available to me. I'm excited about the opportunity to expand my knowledge and contribute to the organization in a meaningful way.

JENNIFER
(impressed)
Max, I like your attitude. I'll be in touch soon with a decision.

INT. APARTMENT LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Sarah sits at her laptop, typing away, a smile on her face. Max enters, carrying a bottle of wine and two glasses.

MAX
(setting down the wine)
Hey, Sarah. I heard back from Jennifer. I got the job.

SARAH
(excitedly)
Max, I'm so happy for you!

They clink glasses and take a sip of the wine, both smiling at each other.

MAX
(leaning back in the chair)
I couldn't have done it without your help, Sarah.

SARAH
(smiling)
I'm just glad that you get the opportunity to make a difference.

MAX
(leaning forward)
And I'm glad that I get to do it with you by my side.

They share a knowing look, their eyes locked in a moment of understanding.

FADE OUT.

End of screenplay.
